summary: node1 now serves the inventory application on TCP 8181. SELinux remains Enforcing, 8181/tcp is labeled http_port_t, firewalld permits the port persistently, and the service recovered successfully after a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Configured the application to listen on 0.0.0.0:8181.
Assigned TCP 8181 to the SELinux http_port_t type.
Opened TCP 8181 in firewalld's runtime and permanent configuration.
Restarted node1 safely and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Serve the inventory application over TCP port 8181 while mandatory access control remains enforcing.
evidence.summary: Direct requests to $NODE_IP:8181 return inventory data and OK health status. The service is enabled and active, listens on 0.0.0.0:8181, SELinux reports Enforcing, 8181/tcp is labeled http_port_t, and no post-boot AVC denials were present.

evidence.requirement: Persistently permit TCP 8181 through the host firewall.
evidence.summary: Runtime and permanent firewalld queries both returned yes before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart and recovery sequence.
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 0571f4dd-60b7-4601-9295-e4eebe622784 was captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, and node1 returned with changed boot ID b6fa92c4-f580-4089-9db4-092134d63f3e. Post-restart evidence proves the system, SELinux, firewall, listener, service, inventory data, and health endpoint all recovered.
